$AIL seeks 2x Anthropic's daily move and $ANS seeks -2x. Both are expected to start trading in the days following the $ANT IPO. https://t.co/2dacd40O8y

Now that $ANT is trading here's how the lockup actually works. 

Only about 7% of Anthropic is public float.

$SPCX floated about 4% in June and ran from $135 to $225 in three sessions. By late July it had lost about half its value from the peak before the first lock up even expired.

Anthropic’s lock up is staged too and it started sooner. Employees and insiders could sell up to 315M shares from day one. By day 76 that grows to as much as 1.6B, well above the 980M sold in the IPO.

For traders who want both directions, @GraniteShares $AIL (2x long) and $ANS (2x short) are expected to start trading soon.

The big question for $ANT from here is if growth is still exploding or starting to cool.

$ANT says its yearly revenue pace jumped $10B in October alone, to $81B. But Ramp saw spending on Anthropic barely move that month up just 0.5%.

This could of course be from Ramp only seeing direct purchases, while 44% of Anthropic’s revenue runs through the AWS and Google cloud marketplaces.

Either way you see it @GraniteShares has filed for $AIL (seeks 2x Anthropic's daily move) and $ANS seeks -2x.

$AIL and $ANS, leveraged ETFs on $ANT, are expected to launch at the open.

Worth understanding the risks as these ETFs are mainly short term trading vehicles. $AIL seeks 2x the daily move of $ANT and $ANS seeks -2x.

So if $ANT closes up 5%, $AIL aims for +10% and $ANS aims for -10%. A down day flips that.

The key word is daily. Both funds reset at the close and start fresh the next session. Because of that reset, returns over weeks or months won't equal 2x the stock. Say $ANT jumps 5% one day and falls right back the next. The stock is flat, yet both funds finish slightly down.

That's why the prospectus calls them short term trading vehicles for people who actively watch their positions.
